title: Rollout Cohort Diff Explorer and Trace-linked Auto-rollback Signals
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a Rollout Cohort Diff Explorer inside Console that enables product and SRE teams to compare canary/A-B cohorts side-by-side across: per-route latency P50/P95/P99, token-level cost, error rate by error class, semantic quality signals (evaluation prompts pass/fail), and request trace samples. The Explorer should support: 1) instant diff views for recent rollouts (last 24h, 7d), 2) drill-through to representative traces and model outputs, 3) significance testing (bootstrap p-values) for metric deltas, 4) configurable auto-rollback triggers (threshold + trend), and 5) a shadow-traffic validation tab that overlays shadow vs production behavior without impacting traffic. Goal: reduce time-to-detect regressions during canary/A-B rollouts from hours to minutes and enable safe automatic rollback when regressions exceed configured tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Console has a new 'Cohort Diff Explorer' page that lists active rollouts and historical rollouts with start/end times.

Users can select two cohorts (control and treatment) and view per-route metric panels: latency P50/P95/P99, errors per 1k requests broken down by class, token cost per request, and a quality score derived from eval prompt pass rates.
Diff panels show absolute and relative deltas with statistical significance indicators (p < 0.05, trend arrows).
Clicking a metric tile opens a trace-linked sample list: each sample shows request metadata, model version, full prompt, model output, and trace link to distributed spans.

Auto-rollback configuration UI allows teams to define policy: metric, comparator (>, <), threshold, sustained window (minutes), and minimum sample size. Policy can be applied per-route or global to the rollout.
Shadow tab shows side-by-side distribution plots for production vs shadow traffic and highlights any behavioral divergence above a configurable JS divergence threshold.
Backend supports query latencies under 2s for a 7-day window for cohorts with up to 10M requests using pre-aggregated rollup tables and an index for (route, model_version, time_bucket).
Unit and integration tests for significance engine, auto-rollback webhook flow, and RBAC checks for viewing rollout data are present and passing.
Documentation and runbook for interpreting diff signals and manual rollback steps are published in Confluence (link included in comments).
notes: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial PRD draft. Motivation: last month a canary introduced a subtle hallucination regression that escaped synthetic evals; surfaced only in production in specific routes. We need faster detection and a clear rollback guard.
2025-02-12 - Marco Rivera: Tech spike planned with ENG infra to validate rollup query performance against 30M recent requests. Spike owners: Priya S. and Omar L.

2025-02-14 - Priya Shah (ENG): Spike results: using a 1-minute time_bucket rollup and precomputed quantile sketches for latency reduces query times by ~6x. Caveat: quantile sketches increase memory; recommended to keep 7-day retention for detailed quantiles and 90-day for coarse aggregates.

2025-02-15 - Design feedback (DES-214): suggested a three-column layout: cohort A metrics, delta center column with significance badges, cohort B metrics. Also proposed colorblind-friendly palettes and compact sparkline visuals for trend context.
2025-02-17 - Marco Rivera: Decided to include a 'representative traces' sampler using stratified sampling by route and response code to avoid bias toward high-volume routes.
2025-02-18 - Security note: viewing raw prompts/outputs must be gated by 'view-sensitive-logs' permission due to possible PII. ENG to add RBAC check and masking option for policy-compliant teams.

2025-02-19 - Omar L. (ENG): Auto-rollback workflow prototype: Console triggers a signed webhook to the rollout controller with reason, metric snapshot, and proposed action. Controller performs optimistic check and executes rollback if guardrails satisfied. Need to add audit log entry with rollback rationale.
2025-02-21 - PM review: Add ability to attach a 'human-in-loop' step before automatic rollback for non-critical regressions (configuration: auto vs auto-with-confirmation).
2025-02-22 - Compliance: For Private customers, ensure rollout telemetry can be routed to customer KMS-backed storage; add option in rollout settings to disable prompt/output storage.
2025-02-24 - Marco Rivera: Implementation branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/7142. Backend schema PR: ENG-2950. Console UI PR: DES-214. Integration tests in ci/rollouts/*.

2025-02-25 - Aisha Kapoor: In Review - requesting engineering estimates for remaining work (metrics retention policy, RBAC plumbing, webhook idempotency). Also asking for sample runbook wording for 'When a rollback triggers'.
implementation_notes: Backend: add 'rollout_event_store' rollups keyed by (route, model_version, cohort_id, time_bucket) with precomputed: count, errors_by_class, token_cost_sum, quantile_sketch(latency).
Significance engine: bootstrap resampling on aggregated samples with configurable iterations (default 1000) and early-stopping when p-value stabilizes.
Trace linking: store exemplar trace_ids per time_bucket + error_class + route for O(1) drill-through retrieval.
Auto-rollback: webhook payload must include checksum of rollout config to prevent out-of-band actions; controller to record audit entry to immutable store.
Query perf: use TTL-based materialized views for 1m/5m rollups and background job to backfill when cohort definitions change.
RBAC: new permission 'rollout.view_sensitive' gating raw prompt/output access; masking default for orgs without approval.
